conventions.convention: SI units; upward vertical coordinate z; reference surface z=0; fixed impermeable bed z=-h; velocity u=∇φ with no added uniform component. Impermeability imposes φ_z=0 at the bed; no-slip is not imposed.
The liquid-to-gas normal is (-ε∇hη,1)/sqrt(1+ε²|∇hη|²); signed curvature is -div_h(ε∇hη/sqrt(1+ε²|∇hη|²)); liquid-minus-gas pressure is γ times this curvature.

Horizontal fields are defined on R²/(L₁Z×L₂Z), with derivatives taken on periodic lifts. The real coefficient fields have total regularity η∈C² and φ∈C³, including continuous one-sided derivative extensions at the bed and reference surface.

Depth, periods, density, gravity magnitude and surface tension are strictly positive. Surface displacement is an unrestricted formal first-order coefficient; optional finite geometry uses a sufficiently small dimensionless scaling on compact time windows.

Nonzero modes have m∈Z²\{(0,0)}, wavevector 2π(m₁/L₁,m₂/L₂), k>0, time factor exp(-iωt), nonzero complex displacement amplitude H, and initially F∈C²([-h,0],C). The square root in the two frequency branches is the positive real square root.

The equations are adopted linear model assumptions; their dispersion and restoring signs are conditional deductions, with no empirical premises, nonlinear approximation bound or empirical-validity conclusion.

load_bearing.statement: On the fixed periodic reference slab, adopt Δ_hφ+φ_zz=0, φ_z(x,-h,t)=0, η_t(x,t)=φ_z(x,0,t), and φ_t(x,0,t)+gη(x,t)-(γ/ρ)Δ_hη(x,t)=0, with the stated positive parameters, regularity and formal first-order interpretation.

For each nonzero integer lattice index and the stated mode definition, a nonzero complex mode exists exactly when ω²=(gk+(γ/ρ)k³)tanh(kh). The right-hand side is positive, and the two frequencies are ω=±sqrt((gk+(γ/ρ)k³)tanh(kh)).

seams_checked.note: The physical postulate reproduces the capillary equations of def-fd-wall-defect-capillary-models with σ=γ, L_x=L₁ and L_y=L₂. Its γ>0 branch is a permitted restriction of σ≥0. The finite reflection construction and kinematic-equation argument reconcile the boundary and mixed regularity conventions. The physical theorem derives its modal result locally and does not overstate or require the separate mathematical energy theorem.

post-fd-boundary-data distinguishes impermeability, (u-w_b)·n=0, from separately selected no-slip, u=w_b. For the fixed bed w_b=0, the capillary postulate correctly specializes impermeability to φ_z=0 and explicitly omits no-slip. Both suppliers distinguish periodic identifications from physical walls and assert no general solvability.
